name: Fern Print
line: A Victorian scientific book in EB Garamond with small caps and old-style figures: a frontispiece (Plate I, Bradbury's nature print of Athyrium filix-femina) faces the title page, chapters II–V carry a drop cap, a ruled tally and sidenotes for sources, the explorers' networks are printed in fern green as Figs. 1 and 2, and every plate grows in from stem to tip as it enters view.
notes: The Bradbury scans are lifted to white with a CSS filter and multiplied onto the page so only the fern prints; the network drawings are used as CSS masks filled with fern green. The stem-to-tip growth is a clip-path reveal; a few lines of JavaScript hold it until each lazy image has loaded, and it is skipped with reduced motion or JavaScript off. Section numbers II–V and plate numbers are page furniture, not content. EB Garamond covers Cyrillic; Chinese falls back to system fonts.
